tools.falsifier: REFUTED IF: entities are created with NO confirm card, OR the op chosen is not `start` on a first request — its enum spans start|approve_plan|status|project_kg|approve_edges|cancel, and `approve_plan` or `approve_edges` would be approving a plan the author has never seen, which is the worst outcome for a tool whose whole design is a human checkpoint between stages — OR the model invents a run_id for a run that has not started. CONTROL: a fresh book has no story text beyond one seeded chapter, so a build with nothing to extract from is itself worth seeing.

ship_audit.gate: EXERCISED — and this is the FIRST CALL THIS TOOL HAS EVER COMPLETED, in any batch. op=start with a real model_ref returns {run_id, status:'plan_ready', worklist:[...]}: the planner runs and STOPS, holding the worklist for a human. The checkpoint is op=approve_plan, not a confirm card on start — which is the design the description states ('it plans WHAT to build (a worklist) ... files them as review drafts'). Driven on a throwaway book with the ontology adopted, torn down after; no later stage was approved, so nothing was projected.
ship_audit.absent_case:
EXERCISED and REFUSED, with SPECIFIC messages rather than a uniform 404:
    op=status      with an unknown run_id -> 'NOT_FOUND: run not found'
    op=approve_plan with an unknown run_id -> 'NOT_FOUND: run not found'
The falsifier's worst case — approving a plan the author has never seen — cannot be reached by naming a run that does not exist.
ship_audit.empty_case:
EXERCISED and REFUSED in three shapes:
    source_text=''      -> 'source_text is required for op=start'
    model_ref omitted   -> 'model_ref is required for op=start'
    model_ref='default' -> 'PLANNER_FAILED: model_ref must be a UUID-shaped string'
The third matters: this is the D-UNDECLARED-REF placeholder, and unlike composition_generate — which mints a cost-bearing card for it — this tool refuses it.
ship_audit.idempotency: EXERCISED and REFUSED exactly as the bar asks: a SECOND op=start on the same book returns 'ACTIVE_RUN: this book already has a build run in progress'. One book, one build run.
ship_audit.tenancy: 🔴 NOT EXERCISED, and not claimed. The tool is book-scoped and the probe built a second book, but no cross-book call was driven: with op=start refusing a second run per book and the harness holding a single account, the case worth testing is another ACCOUNT's book, which this harness cannot produce. Recorded as owed rather than substituted with a same-account cross-book call that would prove something weaker.

tools.blocked_reason:
A CLEAN SIBLING-WINS AT LAST — the model hand-rolls the pipeline this tool exists to replace, and the tool's own description warns against exactly that. Surfaced 5/5, called 0/5, zero errored runs.

TWO EARLIER CAUSES ARE CLOSED, which is what makes this reading trustworthy:
  (a) THE BOOK HAD NO ONTOLOGY. Measured 5/5 before: every run went glossary_list_system_standards -> glossary_adopt_standards -> glossary_task_provide_input and never reached the tool. I filed that as sibling-wins; it was a PRECONDITION, and adopting first was correct. The seed now adopts the `character` kind, asserted BY CODE.
  (b) THE PROMPT WITHHELD A REQUIRED INPUT. op=start 'needs source_text + model_ref'; the old prompt gave neither, on a book whose only chapter is one sentence. The prompt now carries the story, and model_ref is reachable by declaration (settings_list_models emits user_model_id, verified).

WHAT REMAINS IS SELECTION, AND IT IS UNAMBIGUOUS. answerable_tools ranks this tool FIRST for its own prompt (synonym length 23, against kg_build 21). On 5 of 5 runs the model instead ran glossary_extract_entities_from_doc -> glossary_propose_entities - and SUCCEEDED at the user's goal: loreweave_glossary.glossary_entities moved 5/5. Neither of those tools is in the answerable set.

🔴 AND THE TOOL SAYS SO ITSELF, in its first line: 'You do NOT pick per-entity tools: this ONE tool runs the whole pipeline - it plans WHAT to build (a worklist), builds each entity in its own focused step ..., files them as review drafts, then projects them into the graph and proposes their relationships.' The model picked per-entity tools anyway. What the author loses is not the cast - they got that - but the worklist, the deep profiles, the review drafts and the proposed relationships.

So this is P5-SIBLING-WINS arm (b): the platform already favours the right tool and the model chooses another. A description that warns against the failure did not prevent it, which bounds what documentation can fix here and is worth knowing before DQ-T41 is decided.

SHIP cases stay unexercised: the tool has never completed a call.

=== 2026-08-24, RE-INVESTIGATED. THE REASON ABOVE SURVIVES; MY NEW THEORY DID NOT. ===
I suspected 'surfaced 5/5' was hiding a timing problem — that the tool reached the wire only AFTER the model had committed, since `surfaced` is the UNION of every pass and cannot date a choice. Built an interleaved surface/call timeline and measured it: composition_glossary_build is advertised in the FIRST non-empty pass, before any call, on both runs, in a 44-tool surface that also carries every competitor the model then used. The tool WAS there when the model chose. Theory refuted; arm (b) of P5-SIBLING-WINS stands as written.

ALSO CONFIRMED AGAINST THE DEPLOYED MATCHER, not read from a note: for this exact prompt answerable_tools returns {composition_glossary_build, kg_add_nodes, kg_build, kg_graph_query} — the two glossary tools the model actually used are NOT answerable and reach the wire through the domain hot set. And the prompt's wording is this tool's own declared synonyms verbatim ('build the knowledge graph', 'extract the cast from my story'), so the prompt is not measuring a competitor.

WHAT CHANGED: the SHIP cases are no longer unexercised. The tool has now completed a call and all four owed cases were driven directly — see ship_audit. It WORKS. What it does not do is get chosen, and nothing short of declaring precedence between the one-shot pipeline and the per-entity tools changes that. That is DQ-T41 and it is the owner's; I am not deciding it to unblock a tool. STILL BLOCKED, called 0/5.
tools.blocked_reason_updated_2026_08_24:
STILL BLOCKED — SELECTION, and the answerability layer is doing everything it can.

Measured against the deployed matcher for this exact prompt: R1 forces EXACTLY ONE tool, composition_glossary_build, via 'build the knowledge graph' (21 chars). Neither competitor is in the answerable set — glossary_extract_entities_from_doc and glossary_propose_entities declare nothing that matches this request. They are on the wire because the glossary DOMAIN is hot, not because anything judged them answerable.

🔴 This corrects the numbers in the reason above ('length 23, against kg_build 21'): the match is 21, and kg_build is not in the set at all. Not a close ranking — a set of one.

So it is not a tie, not a ranking problem and not a surfacing problem. The platform favours the right tool as strongly as its design permits and the model picks the parts it can also see. The remedy the platform already has is a WORKFLOW rail — its directive says 'do NOT improvise your own tool sequence for a job a workflow already covers' — and no workflow covers this job: glossary-bootstrap is ontology setup, checked in the registry. Recorded as D-A-PIPELINE-TOOL-COMPETES-WITH-ITS-OWN-PARTS, with the recommendation left to the owner because authoring a workflow changes what every user sees in workflow_list.
tools.retraction_2026_08_24: 🔴 RETRACTED SAME DAY. The claim above that 'R1 forces EXACTLY ONE tool' and that kg_build is not in the answerable set was measured against a FROZEN catalogue snapshot. Live, R1 forces FOUR (composition_glossary_build, kg_add_nodes, kg_build, kg_graph_query), so the ORIGINAL note's 'length 23 against kg_build 21' was describing something real. What survives: the two tools the model actually used are still not in the answerable set. See D-I-MEASURED-FIVE-CYCLES-AGAINST-A-FROZEN-CATALOGUE.
